name: Conservation Partners Legacy (CPL) Grant Program
summary: Minnesota state matching grants for nonprofits and public bodies that restore, enhance or protect prairies, wetlands, forests and fish and wildlife habitat. In fiscal year 2027 all money goes to projects in the Twin Cities metro area and the state's largest cities.

geography.label: Minnesota: the seven-county Twin Cities metro area, Duluth, Rochester and St. Cloud

pool.label: FY2027
pool.note: Split between the Metro and Expedited Conservation grant cycles, across several rounds

reporting: Grantees file an accomplishment report by 31 December of each year the grant is active, updated cumulatively until it becomes the final report, and prepare an ecological restoration and management plan with the first payment request.

steps: Online application, if Metro Round 2 opens

eligibility.rule: Total project costs do not exceed $1,000,000
The project manager is affiliated with the recipient and knowledgeable about the proposal
Names a project manager and fiscal contact, neither of whom can be the land manager
Fee-title acquisitions allow public hunting and fishing in all open seasons unless law provides otherwise

documents: Signed Land Manager Review and Approval Form
Public Waters Project Form, if the project is in public waters
Permanent conservation easement documentation, for work on private lands
Partner commitment letters, if partner funds are used as match
Preliminary engineering design and plans, for construction projects
Financial documentation, for NGOs requesting over $25,000

calls.label: FY2027 Expedited Conservation Projects, Round 2
calls.note: Grants of $5,000 to $75,000 for restoration and enhancement only. Later rounds close on 11 January, 8 March and 10 May 2027, or when funds run out.

calls.label: FY2027 Metro grants, Round 2

status.quote: January 1, 2027: Round 2 application system opens if funds remain.

opens.quote: January 1, 2027: Round 2 application system opens if funds remain.

calls.note: Held only if funds remain after Round 1.

pool.quote: $13.1 Million is available for CPL grants for FY2027.

applicant_types.quote: Registered 501 c(3) nonprofit organizations and government entities are eligible for CPL funding. Private individuals and for-profit organizations may not apply.

geography.quote: Projects must be located within the 7- county metro area or within city limits of cities with a population of 50,000 or greater (Duluth, Rochester, St. Cloud).

access.quote: Applications for Round 1 of the Metro and Expedited Conservation Project (ECP) grant cycles will be accepted online beginning August 1, 2026.

window.quote: Completed applications will be pulled for review every two months on the following days at 4:00 pm

amount.quote: provide competitive matching grants from $5,000 up to $500,000 to local, regional, state, and national non-profit organizations and government entities

co_finance_required.quote: A 10% match of non-state funds is required for all grants. The match may be cash or in-kind resources.

reporting.quote: Accomplishment Reports must be submitted by December 31 of each year that the grant is active. The Accomplishment Report form is designed to be cumulative and updated each year until it becomes the Final Report.

effort.quote: If funding remains, Round 2 will open on January 1, 2027 and close on February 16, 2027 at 4:00 PM, CST.
CPL staff will review all applications for completeness and eligibility.
Technical review of applications will be performed by a habitat-specific Technical Review Committee (TRC) and by DNR Regional Directors.

The Division Directors of DNR Fish and Wildlife, Ecological and Water Resources, and Forestry will review all applications and make a final recommendation to the DNR Commissioner based on the following:
The Commissioner of the Department of Natural Resources must give final approval as to which projects to fund

eligibility.quote: Total project cost may not exceed $1,000,000.
The Project Manager must be affiliated with the grant recipient's organization and be knowledgeable about biological, partnership, and administrative aspects of the proposal.
Applications must have a project manager, land manager, and a fiscal contact. The project manager and fiscal contact may be the same person, but neither can also be the Land Manager.
Lands acquired in fee title must be open to the public for hunting and fishing during all open seasons unless otherwise provided by law.
Registered 501 c(3) nonprofit organizations and government entities are eligible for CPL funding.
Projects funded with FY27 funds must be completed by June 30, 2030.

co_finance.quote: The match amount is determined by multiplying the grant amount requested by 10%.

after_award.quote: Accomplishment Reports must be submitted by December 31 of each year that the grant is active.
A Final Accomplishment Report must be submitted with the final payment request by July 25, 2030.

documents.quote: Each applicant must submit a completed Land Manager Review and Approval Form, including the Natural Heritage Database Review section, signed by the Land Manager or Easement Holder and uploaded electronically to the application. For work on private lands, the permanent conservation easement documentation must be uploaded.
Projects occurring within public waters must submit a Public Waters Project Form in addition to the Land Manager Review and Approval Form.
Match funds from partners must be supported with letters of commitment.

Any projects requesting money for construction activities (water control structures, etc.) must have preliminary engineering design and plans completed for the project prior to application submission. These plans are necessary to provide an accurate cost estimate and fully developed scope of work. All plans must be submitted with the application.
Nongovernmental organizations requesting over $25,000 are required to submit financial documentation to meet the State Grant Policy 08-06.
